brief.scope: Work order: the uncited-correction gate. The requirements are the ten numbered Contract items of .dev/ladder-inputs/scope-gate-20260910.md, tracked in this snapshot at the ref; read it and .dev/ladder-inputs/scope-discipline.md WHOLE from the snapshot tree. Nothing else is a requirement. Refuse at mint any write job that answers reviewer findings unless every finding it answers is named by key, disposed in the findings ledger, and the disposition cites the numbered contract item it violates; the ladder stops before its fix stages instead of correcting. No override. Boundaries as listed there; do not widen them.

findings.claim: Contract items 3 and 4 are still contradictory at the handoff: both tracked plans direct the ledger slice to implement the colon-greedy citation regex, while the dispatch contract pins the corrected regex. The plan's prescribed evidence therefore captures the trailing colon as part of the path, so following its exact disposition remedy remains uncited with no override.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re
from pathlib import Path
old=r"contract item (?P<item>[1-9][0-9]*) of (?P<path>[^\s;,]+)"
new=r"contract item (?P<item>[1-9][0-9]*) of (?P<path>[^\s;,:]+)"
plans=[Path('.dev/ladder-inputs/plan-gate-20260910.md'),Path('.dev/ladder-inputs/plan-gate-contracts.md')]
assert all(old in p.read_text() for p in plans)
assert new in Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md').read_text()
m=re.search(old,'contract item 3 of .dev/ladder-inputs/scope-gate-20260910.md: found-text missing')
print(m['path'],Path(m['path']).is_file())
assert m['path'].endswith(':') and not Path(m['path']).is_file()
PY

findings.claim: Contract item 3 requires an exact executable remedy, but both plans still print the real finding key unquoted and prescribe a key validator of `^\S+#[1-9][0-9]*$`. That validator admits shell substitutions, so an operator following the required remedy can execute text embedded in a key outside the job; quoting only the later contract did not repair the plans that direct the next slices.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re,subprocess
from pathlib import Path
plan=Path('.dev/ladder-inputs/plan-gate-20260910.md').read_text()
assert r'^\S+#[1-9][0-9]*$' in plan
assert 'disposition <key>\n<disposition>' in plan
key='$(uname)#1'
assert re.fullmatch(r'\S+#[1-9][0-9]*',key)
out=subprocess.check_output(['bash','-c',f"printf '<%s>\\n' {key}"],text=True).strip()
print(out)
assert out!='<$(uname)#1>' and out.endswith('#1>')
PY

findings.claim: Contract item 4 requires a numbered item of a scope file, but the planned validator accepts any file below the repository root that contains a numbered line. A citation to `docs/verified-couplings.md` therefore satisfies every declared mechanical check and can unlock a correction without citing its work-order scope.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import re
from pathlib import Path
grammar=r"contract item (?P<item>[1-9][0-9]*) of (?P<path>[^\s;,:]+)"
assert grammar in Path('ops/devlane/dispatch/CONTRACT.md').read_text()
m=re.search(grammar,'contract item 1 of docs/verified-couplings.md')
f=Path(m['path']).resolve(); root=Path.cwd().resolve()
numbered=any(re.match(r'^\s*'+m['item']+r'\.\s',line) for line in f.read_text().splitlines())
print(m['path'],f.is_relative_to(root),numbered)
assert f.is_relative_to(root) and numbered and not m['path'].startswith('.dev/ladder-inputs/scope-')
PY

findings.claim: Contract item 1 classifies `adjudicate` and `sweep` as review jobs, but the ledger importer excludes both and the planned ledger slice does not add them. Findings from those review records cannot acquire ledger rows, so their corrections are permanently refused under contract items 3 and 6.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
import ast,json
from pathlib import Path
tree=ast.parse(Path('ops/conductor/tools/findings.py').read_text())
jobs=ast.literal_eval(next(n.value for n in tree.body if isinstance(n,ast.Assign) and any(isinstance(x,ast.Name) and x.id=='REVIEW_JOBS' for x in n.targets)))
missing={'check-tests','security-audit','adversarial-review','adjudicate','sweep'}-set(jobs)
rows=[]
for p in Path('.dev/records/dispatches').glob('*.json'):
 r=json.loads(p.read_text()); findings=((((r.get('result') or {}).get('envelope') or {}).get('findings') or []))
 if r.get('job') in missing and findings: rows.append((r['id'],r['job'],len(findings)))
section=Path('.dev/ladder-inputs/plan-gate-20260910.md').read_text().split('### Slice 2 — `ledger-gate`',1)[1].split('### Slice 3',1)[0]
print(sorted(missing),rows[:5])
assert missing=={'adjudicate','sweep'} and rows and 'REVIEW_JOBS' not in section
PY

findings.claim: Contract item 1 says `--follows` names a record, but the planned gate interpolates each ID into `<records>/<id>.json` without a one-component or containment check, while current record validation checks only that `follows` is a list. An absolute ID is accepted and makes the new gate read outside `.dev/records/dispatches` and the job boundary.

import record

print(candidate,candidate.is_relative_to(records))

findings.claim: Contract item 1 also requires the followed object to be a record, but the plan says `correction.py` reads only its `job` field and never validates the record or binds its internal ID to the requested ID. A forged `{"job":"plan"}` is enough to classify a write as a non-correction even though the repository's record validator rejects it, bypassing the gate by trusting unchecked record output.

Contract item 5 requires `disposed_at` to precede mint, but the plan records both values only to whole seconds and accepts `disposed_at <= stamp`. A disposition written after mint within the same second compares equal and is accepted by the already-started attempt.
findings.reproduce:
python3 - <<'PY'
from datetime import datetime,timezone
from pathlib import Path
plan=Path('.dev/ladder-inputs/plan-gate-20260910.md').read_text()
assert 'disposed_at <= stamp' in plan
mint=datetime(2026,9,10,12,0,0,100000,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
disposed=datetime(2026,9,10,12,0,0,900000,tzinfo=timezone.utc)
wire=lambda d:d.isoformat(timespec='seconds').replace('+00:00','Z')
print(mint.isoformat(),disposed.isoformat(),wire(disposed)<=wire(mint))
assert disposed>mint and wire(disposed)<=wire(mint)
PY

envelope.note: Covered argv/shell, SQL/template, secrets, path/ref containment, permission/sandbox records, vendor-output trust, and supply-chain deltas. The repository secret scanner was clean across all 26 changed files; all 10 added dispatch records passed record validation and their recorded sandbox labels matched their argv; both focused document-pin suites passed. No SQL/template, credential, sandbox-label, or supply-chain finding was found. The live gate is not in this slice, so runtime gate behavior and external network/vendor enforcement could not be exercised. The session store was not read.
